subject: Re: MAP & evaluation cadence — deployment mode and geo ask
messages:
From: Emma Jones <emma.jones@pulseiq.com>
To: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>; Samir Rao <samir.rao@pulseiq.com>
Date: Thu, 20 May 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: MAP kickoff + geo & deployment preference questions

Hi Mina,

Thanks again for the demo yesterday — the team was impressed with Redwood's latency and the cost transparency. We want to move from discovery to a more formal mutual action plan so we can lock a Q3 go-live target. A few things we need to resolve before committing:

- Data residency: some of our PII must remain in US regions for now; EU is for non-PII only.
- Deployment mode question: for production, we are evaluating Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private (on-prem/VPC). Cost, time-to-live, and security are the deciding factors.
- Eval plan: we need a POC that demonstrates throughput at our average request size (~1.2k tokens) and a perf snapshot for 99th %ile latency.
- Procurement: our standard procurement/contract review takes ~6 weeks; can Redwood work with that cadence?

Can you send a proposed MAP with milestones, owners, and a recommended deployment path (including fallback plan for EU users) so we can align internally? Attaching our RFP attachments for context.

Target internal goal: have MAP agreed and procurement initiated by end of June so we can aim for a Sept 1st production readiness target.

Cheers,
Emma
Emma Jones
VP Product, PulseIQ
emma.jones@pulseiq.com

From: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>

Date: Fri, 21 May 2027 10:04:00 -0700
Subject: Re: MAP kickoff + geo & deployment preference questions

Hi Emma — thanks for the clear asks and the RFP pack. Attached is a first-pass MAP (PulseIQ_MAP_v1.xlsx) and a short SOC2 intake form we typically use during procurement. High level recommendations up front:

- Recommended production path: Dedicated pool in US (for PII + predictable throughput) with a Hosted EU read-only edge for demo/POC and lower-latency read-serving for EU users.
  - Why: Dedicated gives control over placement, predictable latency at scale, and isolation for regulatory needs. Hosted EU lets us avoid on-prem procurement delays for customer-facing demos.
- Private (on-prem) is achievable but will add 8–12 weeks for packaging + legal + operational onboarding; we should treat Private as a longer-term commitment if PulseIQ needs an air-gapped option.

MAP (proposed milestones & owners):
1) Week 0 (by 2027-05-28): MAP sign — owners: Mina (Redwood AE), Emma (PulseIQ Prod) — agree on region and deployment lane.
2) Week 1–2 (by 2027-06-11): SOW/technical spec + perf targets — owner: Karthik (tech lead).
3) Week 3–6 (by 2027-07-09): POC run (dedicated test pool + hosted EU edge) — owner: Karthik + PulseIQ eng. Acceptance: sustained 500 TPS equivalent at 1.2k tokens and 99th %ile latency < 300ms for gen paths.
4) Week 6–10 (by 2027-08-13): Procurement & legal — owner: Emma + Laura (CS/AM) — finalize terms and SOC/KMS details.
5) Week 11 (by 2027-08-20): Staging cutover and production runbook — owner: Ops + PulseIQ.
6) Target prod-ready: 2027-09-01 (soft go-live).

Please review the attached MAP sheet — it has checkboxes for each acceptance criterion and a column for Redwood deliverables. A couple of immediate asks for PulseIQ to speed alignment:
- Confirm that Dedicated in US is acceptable for prod and that EU can be served from Hosted for now.
- Share your procurement lead and legal contact so we can surface the SOC2 and KMS requirements early.
- Confirm any hard blackout dates in July/Aug.

I'll loop Rishi in for a cost/throughput estimate once you confirm the acceptance numbers.

Best,
Mina Haddad
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
mina_haddad@redwood.com
Attachments: PulseIQ_MAP_v1.xlsx; SOC2_Request_Form.pdf
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
To: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 24 May 2027 14:22:00 -0700
Subject: INTERNAL: Tech + cost read on PulseIQ MAP (re: recommendation)

Mina — quick internal note while we prepare the cost model. Replying inline to your proposal: 

- Dedicated (US) for prod: Agree. Provides us dedicated GPU capacity and predictable token pricing. Procurement will need explicit commitment size (e.g., reserved v100/h100 hours) to lock price — we should propose a 12-month commit with staged invoicing to soften PulseIQ's procurement ask.
- Hosted (EU) edge for POC/demo: Good short-term tradeoff. Hosting EU endpoints on our hosted fleet avoids spinning dedicated EU capacity for the POC. We should clarify data flow: EU demo traffic should be routed to EU-hosted models and not persisted to US buckets unless PulseIQ allows cross-border.
- Private/on-prem: Not recommended for initial launch unless PulseIQ can accept an extra 8–12 week runway. On-prem packaging adds integration work (KMS, audit logs) and requires access to their infra team for validation.

Technical caveats and action items for acceptance tests:
1) KV cache priming: For throughput tests use realistic session locality; we should script warmup sequences to avoid cold-start token inflation.
2) 99th %ile latency target: depends heavily on model selection (we should map model choice to acceptance; propose two model tiers to test: baseline open model + quantized variant).
3) Throughput sizing: I'll run a cost estimate with both continuous batching enabled and a conservative active-token cap. Rishi — can you draft a 90/120-day cost projection for Dedicated pool (US-east) vs Hosted mixed?

Rishi: see note below — I'll need the following to finalize numbers: PulseIQ expected monthly token volume (gen vs embedding split), concurrency targets (avg vs peak), and preferred model families.

Quote of Mina's note for context:
> MAP (proposed milestones & owners):
> 1) Week 0 (by 2027-05-28): MAP sign — owners: Mina (Redwood AE), Emma (PulseIQ Prod) — agree on region and deployment lane.

We'll attach the cost sheet to the MAP and circulate.

Thanks — Karthik

--

Subject: MAP v1 — confirmation and next steps (Dedicated US + Hosted EU for POC)

Emma — thanks for the quick turnaround internally yesterday. Per our internal cost review and your constraints, here's the updated and agreed near-term plan: 

Agreed deployment lanes (near-term):
- Production: Dedicated GPU pool in US-east (PII stays in-region) — target commit: 6–12 month reserved capacity (flex invoicing option available).
- POC/demo: Hosted EU endpoints (no PII persistence to US) — will be used for demos and EU customer acceptance only.
- Private/on-prem: deferred — we'll include a technical appendix with estimated 10-week additional lead time if PulseIQ wants to go this route later.

Updated MAP timeline (finalized):
- 2027-05-28: MAP v1 issued and owners confirmed (this thread).
- 2027-06-04: Tech spec + model selection (Karthik) — includes perf targets and chosen model tiers.
- 2027-06-18 to 2027-07-16: POC execution window (two-week runs with measurement windows).
- 2027-07-16 to 2027-08-13: Procurement & contract finalization (Laura + Emma).
- 2027-08-20: Staging cutover rehearsal.
- 2027-09-01: Soft prod launch.

Immediate asks for PulseIQ to unblock us:
1) Confirm that the Dedicated US production lane is acceptable.
2) Provide token volume proxy (monthly estimate) and peak concurrency window so Rishi can finalize cost.
3) Share procurement contact and any legal playbooks (standard NDAs or required clauses).

I'll upload the MAP v1 and the cost appendix to the Drive folder and seed a HubSpot deal record (link below). If PulseIQ is ready, we can schedule a 30-minute MAP sign meeting next Tuesday (2027-05-31) to confirm owners and start the SOW work. I'll also include a pre-filled DocuSign cover letter you can use to kick procurement.

Thanks — looking forward to getting this moving.
